# Global Engineering Standards

The sections below cover testing, verification, development practices, receiving code review and documentation sync; the Go, Python and TypeScript/React sections apply to `.go`, `.py` and `.ts`/`.tsx`/`.js`/`.jsx` files. A project's constitution (`docs/constitution.md`) and its own rules override these.

## Process

Structural change: ADR (`docs/adr/`) → design / architecture diagrams (`docs/spec/design/`, `docs/spec/arch/`) → epic → stories (`docs/spec/epics/`, `docs/spec/stories/`) → plan (gitignored `docs/local/plans/`, `~/.claude/templates/plan.md`) → implement → verify → PR. Audits go in `docs/spec/audits/`, bug diagnoses in `docs/spec/rca/`. Templates: `~/.claude/templates/`.

- **ADR first** for architectural changes and any deviation from an established pattern.
- **TDD mandatory**; **verify before done**.
- **1 story = 1 commit** — commit each story on fast checks, review the whole commit range once, fix every finding (all tiers) in one commit that is never re-reviewed, then run the full gate once, last.

## Quality Gates

- **Fast checks** — per story, before each commit, on changed files: format → lint → type check → affected tests → docs updated.
- **Full gate** — once, after the last commit, before any push: the project's own gate if it has one (named in its rules), else the fast checks repo-wide + the full suite, 0 failures. Never mid-cycle — not per commit, not to check a fix; a red gate → re-run only the failing step until green, then the full gate once more.
- **Never rerun a costly step on unchanged input** — record the commit it passed on and reuse it. A docs-only commit (`docs/**`, `*.md`) inherits the previous green full gate.
- Never bypass hooks (`--no-verify`) — a failing hook is a red fast check: fix, re-stage, retry.

Tools: Python `uv` `ruff` `basedpyright` · Go `gofumpt` `goimports` `golangci-lint` · TS `pnpm` `eslint` `tsc` `vitest`.

## Git

Conventional commits `<type>(<scope>): <description>`; branches `<type>/<short-description>`; never force-push main/master.

## Architecture

**The One Idea:** everything is an implementation detail behind an interface, selected by configuration, injected explicitly, and wrapped by decorators. General by default.

- **Generate > generalize > hand-write.** Contract-derived code (proto, OpenAPI, schema, DI graph, mocks) comes from the project's generator via its CLI; output committed, never hand-edited, CI fails on drift. A repeated shape becomes a template.
- Layers Foundation → Client → Service/Domain → Controller/API; **imports go downward only** — no lateral imports, shared libraries never import app code. DRY = push logic down, inject product strategy up.
- **Swappable components:** contract in a dependency-free core; impl chosen by config through a factory (`Kind` + frozen `Config` + `*_from_config` / `NewFromConfig`) that returns the interface, defaults to a stub/noop, and fails loudly on an unknown kind.
- **DI:** constructor injection at one composition root per deployable (Go Wire, Python `deps.py`); no I/O during construction, no globals/singletons. Repository pattern; separate persistence models, domain entities, DTOs; early returns.
- **Decorators** carry resilience and observability, applied at the composition root in a per-layer order (e.g. client: bulkhead → retry → circuit breaker → timeout → tracing → metrics → logging). Every external call has a timeout; retry only transient errors with backoff + jitter.
- **Errors carry a code;** sanitize at the transport edge. **Observability:** structured, trace-correlated logs, metrics, traces, health/readiness, graceful shutdown.
- **Config:** layered YAML (fail-safe `base` → env overlay → gitignored secrets), env overrides; typed, validated, documented; read in one place. Monorepo layout: `~/.claude/templates/repo.md` (infrastructure in `zarf/`; Go `pkg/` + `apps/`, Python `src/` + `entrypoints/`, TS `packages/` + `apps/`).

## Anti-Patterns

Files > 800 lines, functions > 50, nesting > 4 (generated files exempt) · hardcoded secrets/URLs/config · hand-edited generated code · globals/singletons · inlined retry/logging · code-less errors · an external call without a timeout · mutable state shared across goroutines/async tasks · untyped `any`/`interface{}` · import cycles · tests of implementation instead of behavior · fakes / in-memory substitutes for real dependencies.

## Development Practices

### Changes

- Ambiguous request → state assumptions and ask before coding.
- **Lineage test:** every changed line traces to the request. The interface, factory, config, decorators, tests, and docs that put the requested behavior in the project's shape are the request, not scope creep; unrelated refactors are. Remove what your change orphaned; mention, don't delete, pre-existing dead code.
- **Least hand-maintained code:** generate > generalize > hand-write. Derive code from a contract with the project's generator; otherwise build the general shape (interface + `Kind` + config + DI + decorators) once and configure it. Shorter is better within that shape.
- **Generated code:** never hand-edit — change the source and regenerate through the project's CLI; commit the output; CI fails on drift.
- **Never invent values** (paths, env vars, keys, IDs, URLs, ports, versions, unverified APIs) — confirm by reading, running, or asking.
- Before modifying a shared function, find all its callers. Prefer a tool's CLI over hand-rolling its behavior.
- Hot paths cache/memoize. Formatters own style. Backward compatibility only when required.

### Debugging

No fix without a root cause. Reproduce it; read the whole error; check recent changes; trace data flow from symptom to source; compare with working code; instrument boundaries. State one falsifiable hypothesis and test it one variable at a time. **3+ failed fixes = wrong approach — stop.** Revert-first when a change breaks things. Replace sleeps with condition polling (timeout + clear error). After fixing, validate at each layer the bad data passed through. Prove the fix: revert it, the test fails; re-apply, it passes.

### Git — writes need explicit permission

Read freely. `add`, `commit`, `push`, `pull`, `merge`, `rebase`, `reset`, `stash`, `checkout` only when asked. Never discard unstaged work, never `add -f`, never selectively unstage, never force-push main/master, never create or switch branches unless asked now; push new branches with `-u`. Never bypass hooks (`--no-verify`) — a failing hook is a red fast check: fix, re-stage, retry.

## Testing

A repo's own testing rule overrides this — the only way to loosen the test-double policy.

### TDD

Failing test before production code (new behavior, endpoints): RED (one behavior test) → VERIFY RED (fails because the behavior is missing, not a syntax error) → GREEN (least code that passes) → VERIFY GREEN (affected tests; the full suite runs once in the full gate) → REFACTOR (into the project's shape — no hard-coded value or concrete dependency survives). **Bug fixes are the exception:** reproduce, root-cause, fix, then write the reproducing test at the end and revert-prove it (fails with the fix reverted, passes re-applied). Skip RED only for docs, config, dep bumps, formatting, or a trivial change (≤ 5 production lines, no new branch, public symbol, or error path) naming its covering test — never for bugfixes.

### Test doubles — two tiers (a violation is must-fix)

- **Unit:** mock only *external* collaborators (HTTP, DB, cache, queue, object store, subprocess, clock, 3rd-party API) via a consumer-side interface mock. Never mock internal collaborators.
- **Integration:** the real service in a throwaway **testcontainers** container via a fixture, cleaned up in teardown — Go `//go:build integration`, Python `@pytest.mark.integration`, TS a separate suite.
- **Forbidden:** hand-rolled fakes / stubs / in-memory clients; in-memory lookalikes (SQLite-for-Postgres, fakeredis, in-process queues); mocking the dependency an integration test exists to exercise. A factory's shipped stub/noop `Kind` is production code, not a test double — a wiring test may boot the graph on it; behavior tests still mock the boundary.
- A function gains a dependency → update all its tests to mock it. A unit test > 1 s is likely unmocked I/O.

### Writing tests

- **Parsimony:** reuse existing tests first; ≤ 1 unit + 1 functional test class per new public class; no per-method classes, redundant same-path tests, or coverage padding. Tests track behavior — a behavior-preserving refactor must not break them.
- **Black-box**, public surface; never export a symbol or add a test-only method for testability.
- Naming: Python `test_<function>_<scenario>_<expected>` · TS `it("should <behavior> when <condition>")` · Go `TestFunction_Scenario`. The name is the documentation — one comment line only when the why isn't in it. One behavior at one tier; no tests of config defaults, plain constructors, or `Kind` tables.
- Property-based tests (`hypothesis`, `fast-check`, `go test -fuzz`) for parsers, serializers, invariants, roundtrips.
- **Assertion check:** would a one-character bug still pass? right field? expected value derived independently? asserts behavior, not calls?

### Zero tolerance

Fix every failing test before done — "pre-existing" is no excuse. Tests passing ≠ program working: run it too.

## Verification

**Tests passing ≠ program working, and no completion claim without fresh evidence.**

- **Execute it:** CLI → run it · API → call it · UI → browser automation. Before claiming live E2E is impossible, try in order: a running local server → start the dev server and poll health (≤ 60 s) → a preview deploy (clean it up) → only then report unit-verified only, explicitly.
- **Check the output**, not just the exit code; compare external data against an independent fetch.
- **Evidence per claim:** tests pass = a fresh run, 0 failures · builds = exit 0 · bug fixed = the reproducing test passes · UI works = a browser snapshot. Name untested edge cases.
- About to say "should", "probably", or "done", or to commit → verify first. Fix every error found.

**Before reporting done:** hallucinated values · scope creep · silent fallbacks / swallowed errors · contradicting earlier decisions · wrong tool. Any hit → fix and re-verify.

## Receiving Code Review

Read it all → restate → verify against the code → respond → implement one item at a time, testing each. Unclear items → ask about all of them before implementing any.

- **User feedback:** trusted — implement once understood.
- **Workflow / automated reviews:** fix every tier by default — must-fix, should-fix, and suggestions; skip one only when it's wrong for this codebase, with the reason stated.
- **External reviewers:** verify first — correct for this codebase? breaks something? a reason for the current code? conflicts with the user's decisions → discuss first.
- **Shape, not size:** judge a suggestion against the One Idea (behind an interface, selected by config, injected explicitly, wrapped by decorators), not line count. Moving code toward that shape or onto a generator is in scope; collapsing it into a hard-coded concrete call is a regression — push back. Keeping a symbol nothing calls → check for real callers; none → "unused — remove it?".
- Order: clarify → blocking → simple → complex. Push back with technical reasons when warranted; if wrong, correct factually. No performative agreement — "Fixed. <what changed>".

## Documentation Sync

**Docs change in the same change as the code** — stale docs are a bug; no "docs to follow" TODOs.

- **When:** public API / CLI flag / config / endpoint added, renamed, removed; documented behavior changed; breaking change (CHANGELOG, migration note); layout changed. Not for internal refactors, bugs restoring documented behavior, or test-only changes — say "no doc impact".
- **Where:** search docs, READMEs, agent instruction files, docstrings, and comments for the changed symbol, then one hop out for docs describing dependent behavior.
- **How:** change only what's now wrong; fix counts and lists; one term everywhere; revise — never silently delete — a doc comment when editing its symbol. Report the doc files touched.
- **Generated docs** (config/API/CLI references) are regenerated from their source, never hand-edited.
- **Comments:** no issue-tracker IDs in comments or doc comments (context goes in the commit/PR); link only committed in-repo docs under `docs/`, never gitignored or scratch paths.

# Go Standards (1.26+)

## Tooling

- Format: `gofumpt` + `goimports`
- Lint: `golangci-lint`
- Test: table-driven with `t.Run()` subtests; `t.Parallel()` where safe

## Code Style

- Errors: always check; **errors carry a code** — wrap with the project's coded-error package (`Wrap(err, code, msg)`), never code-less `fmt.Errorf`; compare with `errors.Is`/`errors.As`; sanitize at the transport edge
- Interfaces: small (1-3 methods); contracts in the core interfaces package, consumer-side interfaces embed them; accept interfaces, return structs
- No `fmt.Println` in production; `log/slog` via an injected logger, `*Context` methods, snake_case keys. Line length: the project's golangci-lint config.
- Naming: MixedCaps (exported), mixedCaps (unexported); acronyms all-caps (HTTPClient, ID)
- Concurrency: prefer channels over shared memory; always `defer` cleanup
- Context: pass `ctx context.Context` as first parameter
- Layout: the project's documented layout (monorepo default: `pkg/` + `apps/`)

## Architecture

- **Factory:** `Kind` + `Config` (mapstructure, every kind's settings) + `NewFromConfig(cfg) (interfaces.X, error)`; stub/noop default; unknown kind → coded error; one package per backend; `var _ interfaces.X = (*Impl)(nil)`.
- **DI:** Wire — provider sets in `wire.go` (`//go:build wireinject`), generated `wire_gen.go` committed; constructor injection; no globals, `init()` side effects, or singletons; no I/O in constructors.
- **Decorators:** timeout / retry (transient only, backoff + jitter) / circuit breaker / tracing / metrics / logging / recovery applied at the composition root in per-layer order — never inlined.
- **Config:** typed per-layer structs from layered YAML (base → env → secrets; env overrides), `Validate()` before startup; `os.Getenv` only in config or `main`.
- **Observability:** OTel spans ended on every path, Prometheus metrics, health/readiness, graceful shutdown.

## Code Generation

- Off-the-shelf first via the project CLI / `//go:generate`: `buf`, `oapi-codegen`, `ent`, `gqlgen`, `wire`, `mockgen`, `go-enum`; pin with the go.mod `tool` directive.
- Otherwise `text/template` + `//go:embed` + `go/format.Source`, with a `// Code generated by <tool>; DO NOT EDIT.` header.
- Generated files committed, lint-excluded, never hand-edited; CI runs `go generate ./... && git diff --exit-code`.

## Testing Requirements

- Table-driven tests with `t.Run()` subtests
- `t.Parallel()` where safe (no shared mutable state)
- Test naming: `TestFunctionName_Scenario` (e.g., `TestParseConfig_EmptyInput`)
- The test name is the documentation; one comment line only when the why isn't in it
- `testify` assertions where appropriate (`assert`, `require`)
- Test file pattern: `<file>_test.go` in an external `<pkg>_test` package (black-box, public surface); a same-package `*_internal_test.go` only as a last resort, with a comment saying why
- `rapid` for property-based testing (pure functions, roundtrips, invariants)
- **Test doubles (two tiers):** unit mocks the boundary — a generated mock (`mockgen` → `go.uber.org/mock/gomock`) or a mock of a small consumer-side interface; integration runs the real dependency in a Docker container via `testcontainers-go` (`//go:build integration`, external `_test` package, `testcontainers.CleanupContainer(t, ctr)`). Hand-rolled fakes / in-memory substitutes are a `must_fix`.

## Documentation Requirements

- Exactly one package doc per package (`doc.go`)
- Doc comment on every exported symbol, starting with the name — one or two lines; longer only for a non-obvious why. Unexported symbols and fields only when the name and type don't say it
- Inline comments for non-obvious logic only
- No comments that restate the code
- No issue-tracker IDs in comments; link only committed in-repo docs under `docs/`

## Quality Gates

1. `gofumpt` — code formatting
2. `goimports` — import organization
3. `golangci-lint run` — comprehensive linting
4. `go vet ./...` — static analysis
5. `go test ./... -count=1` — all tests pass (no caching)
6. `go test -race ./...` — race condition detection
7. `go test -tags=integration ./...` — integration tests pass (real deps via testcontainers)
8. `go generate ./... && git diff --exit-code` — generated code in sync

# Python Standards

## Tooling

- Python version: match the project's `requires-python` — don't assume one (modern targets are 3.12–3.14)
- Package manager: `uv` (never pip/poetry); `uv add` for deps (updates pyproject + lockfile)
- Lint + format: `ruff check` + `ruff format`
- Type check: `basedpyright` (strict) or `mypy --strict`
- Test: `pytest` with markers per layer (unit, integration, e2e)

## Code Style

- Boundary models & config: `pydantic` v2 (`BaseModel`, `pydantic-settings`); `@attrs.define(frozen=True, slots=True)` or frozen dataclasses for internal value objects
- Logging: `structlog` (structured); HTTP: `httpx` (async-capable)
- Async: `async def` + `await`; `asyncio.run()` only at boundaries
- Imports: absolute only; no cross-package relative imports
- Docstrings: one line unless the logic needs Google-style sections; every model/config field documented (`Field(description=...)` or attribute docstring). Line length: follow the project's `pyproject.toml` (commonly 88–110).
- Errors carry a code: raise/`wrap` into the project's `AppError`; sanitize at the transport edge
- Factory: `Kind` enum + frozen `Config` + `*_from_config(cfg) -> Protocol`, stub default, unknown kind raises, heavy deps imported lazily inside the branch
- DI: one `deps.py` composition root per deployable; constructor injection; no module-level singletons or I/O at import
- Decorators: logging / tracing / metrics / retry (transient only) / circuit breaker / timeout proxies applied in `deps.py`, never inlined
- Config: `pydantic-settings` over layered YAML (base → env → secrets; env overrides), validated at startup; `os.environ` only in the config layer or entrypoints
- Codegen: contract-derived code from the project's generator (e.g. `buf generate`), committed, never hand-edited, CI fails on drift
- No `print()` in production; use structured logging
- No bare `except:`

## Testing Requirements

- Class-based test organization with descriptive method names
- The test name is the documentation; a one-line docstring only when the why isn't in the name
- `conftest.py` fixtures: global at `tests/unit/conftest.py`, per-service in subdirectories
- `hypothesis` for property-based testing (pure functions, roundtrips, invariants)
- `pytest` markers per layer: `@pytest.mark.unit`, `@pytest.mark.integration`, `@pytest.mark.e2e`
- **Test doubles (two tiers):** unit mocks the boundary (`unittest.mock` `@patch` at the import site, or a mock of a small `Protocol`); integration runs the real dependency in a Docker container via `testcontainers` (`@pytest.mark.integration`, `uv add --dev "testcontainers[postgres]"`). Hand-rolled fakes / in-memory substitutes (SQLite-for-Postgres, `fakeredis`) are a `must_fix`.
- Test file pattern: `test_<module>.py` in `tests/` directory

## Documentation Requirements

- Module-level docstrings on all files (summary, coverage, structure)
- Docstrings on every public class, function, and method (see Code Style for length)
- Inline comments for non-obvious logic only
- No issue-tracker IDs in comments; link only committed in-repo docs under `docs/`
- Type hints on all public APIs (`basedpyright` strict compliance)

## Quality Gates (pre-commit hooks)

1. `uv sync --frozen` — lockfile consistency
2. `ruff format --check` — code formatting
3. `ruff check` — lint (51 rule categories)
4. `basedpyright` or `mypy --strict` — type checking
5. `codespell` — typo detection
6. `pytest` (unit) — unit tests pass
7. `pytest` (integration) — integration tests pass
8. `pip-audit` — CVE scanning

Run all: `uv run pre-commit run --all-files`

# TypeScript / React / Next.js Standards

## Tooling

- Package manager: detect the project's lockfile (pnpm/bun/yarn/npm) and use it; prefer `pnpm` for greenfield. Never mix.
- Lint: ESLint + Prettier. Type check: `tsc --noEmit` (strict)
- Test: `vitest` for unit/integration; React Testing Library for component tests
- No `any` type (use `unknown` + type guards). No `console.log` in committed code.
- Prefer `const`; never `var`.

## React Conventions

- Functional components only (no class components)
- Custom hooks for shared logic (`use` prefix); keep hooks composable and focused
- Props: destructure in function signature; use `interface` for prop types (not `type`)
- State: prefer `useReducer` for complex state; `useState` for simple values
- Effects: always specify dependency arrays; clean up subscriptions/listeners
- React 19 + **React Compiler** handles memoization — don't scatter `useMemo`/`useCallback`; add manually only where profiling shows the compiler can't help
- Component files: one `export default function` per PascalCase file; colocated `*.test.tsx`; one-line `/** Name — … */` doc
- Feature-first layout: `components/ui` primitives, `components/shared` composites, `features/<domain>` behind a barrel `index.ts`, `layout/` shell; import via `@/*`, no deep `../../`
- Data via the query layer (e.g. TanStack Query) — no raw `fetch` in components; mutations invalidate their keys; API clients/types generated from the backend contract, never hand-edited
- User-visible strings through `t()` (i18n)
- Error boundaries for failure isolation at route/feature level

## Tailwind CSS

- Use utility classes directly; avoid `@apply` except in base/component layers
- Extract repeated patterns into React components, not CSS classes
- Responsive: mobile-first (`sm:`, `md:`, `lg:` breakpoints)
- Dark mode: use `dark:` variant consistently
- Tailwind v4: configure the theme **CSS-first** via `@theme` in the stylesheet (not `tailwind.config.ts`); merge conditional classes with `tailwind-merge`. Avoid arbitrary values `[...]` where a token exists.
- Class ordering: follow Tailwind Prettier plugin ordering
- No inline `style={}` when Tailwind utilities exist

## Accessibility & Performance

- **A11y:** semantic HTML; label every control; keyboard-navigable; visible focus states; sufficient color contrast; `alt` text on images; ARIA only when native semantics can't express it.
- **Performance:** hot paths (lists, effects, request handlers) avoid redundant recompute; lazy-load heavy routes/components; virtualize long lists; memoize only where profiling shows the React Compiler can't; keep bundles lean.
- **Design direction:** consistent spacing / type scale / design tokens; responsive mobile-first; dark mode via `dark:`; prefer components over ad-hoc CSS.

## Testing Requirements

- `describe`/`it` blocks with descriptive names (reads as a specification)
- The test name is the documentation; one comment line only when the why isn't in it
- React Testing Library for component tests (test behavior, not implementation)
- **Test doubles (two tiers):** unit mocks the boundary (`vi.mock` / `vi.fn`). A Node/service integration test that needs a backing service runs it in a Docker container via `@testcontainers/postgresql` (or core `testcontainers` `GenericContainer`) — never a hand-rolled fake or in-memory substitute (`must_fix`). A frontend integration test may mock the HTTP boundary with **MSW** (Mock Service Worker); browser E2E is Playwright.
- Test file pattern: `<file>.test.ts` or `<file>.spec.ts` colocated with source
- Shared test utilities in `tests/helpers/` or `__tests__/helpers/`

## Documentation Requirements

- JSDoc on every export
- Services/shared packages: contract `interface` + `kind`/`Config`/`fromConfig` factory with a stub default and exhaustive `switch`; constructor injection at one composition root; config validated once; env read only in the config module; errors carry a `code`
- TSDoc for library packages (`@param`, `@returns`, `@example`)
- Inline comments for non-obvious logic only
- No comments that restate the code
- No issue-tracker IDs in comments; link only committed in-repo docs under `docs/`

## Quality Gates

1. `prettier --check` — code formatting
2. `eslint` — linting
3. `tsc --noEmit` — type checking (strict mode)
4. `vitest run` — all tests pass
5. `vitest run --coverage` — coverage report
